models.label: Random Forest — Sensor-robust (deployed)
models.narrative: Random Forest — Sensor-robust (deployed) — missingness: CO2 dropped. AUROC 0.9129, sensitivity 0.8874, PPV 0.6378 at threshold 0.43 (5-fold property-level CV, n=250). Flats AUROC 0.8642 vs terraced 0.9047. Deployed model — non-linear, best accuracy and the fairest across property types (flats 0.8642). CONDITIONAL: small residual flat gap to monitor; rank within type.

deployment_questions.q1: At threshold 0.43 sensitivity is 0.8874; misses ~11.3% of cold property-days (6078 of 53982 in held-out CV).
deployment_questions.q2: PPV 0.6378 — a positive flag is right ~64% of the time.
deployment_questions.q3: NPV 0.9435 — an all-clear is right ~94% of the time.
deployment_questions.q4: AUROC 0.9129 — ranks a cold property above a warm one ~91% of the time.
deployment_questions.q5: Per-type AUROC flat 0.8642 / terraced 0.9047 / semi 0.903 / detached 0.8936. Flats weakest — rank within type.
deployment_questions.q6: Uses no CO2, so the 38% MNAR dropout cannot affect it; the broken sensors are flagged for repair separately.
deployment_questions.q7: A false negative leaves a genuinely cold household below 19C for another heating season — a delayed health outcome for vulnerable residents.
deployment_questions.q8: Yes — primary ranking engine, with per-type ranking and a sensor-repair workstream.

models.label: Logistic Regression — Sensor-robust (interpretable baseline)

mechanism.mechanism_verdict: Dropout is only weakly tied to property type.
mechanism.outcome_note: Dropout is only weakly correlated with cold-risk (r=0.0366), so the MNAR-with-respect-to-outcome concern is limited: the broken sensors are mainly a data-integrity issue, not a hidden cold-risk bias.

distribution.note: Observed CO2 std is 63.5; naive mean-imputation drops it to 49.8 (a fake spike at the mean), while per-property interpolation keeps it at 58.5 — closer to reality.

mnar_patterns.name: CO2 sensor dropout concentrated in cold/worse-condition stock
mnar_patterns.mechanism: CO2 hardware fails more often in older, higher-deprivation properties; missingness is correlated with the outcome, so a CO2-dependent model is least reliable for the households most likely to be cold.

mnar_patterns.name: Resident survey MNAR — cold homes respond less and score lower
mnar_patterns.mechanism: Thermal-comfort surveys are ~97% missing and the response is itself informative: colder/higher-deprivation properties respond less often, so observed survey scores over-represent comfortable homes.

split_audit.note: No property reference appears in both folds; lag_temp cannot leak across the split.
